senses.gloss: f. pl. (bucina, βυκάνη) bucinæ, horns used in the Roman camps to proclaim the watches of the day and the night.
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:12:2">Cant. R. to I, 12</cite> he appointed over them (read:) <he>קלאנין בב׳ ושופר</he> (v.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 983">Yalk. Cant. 983</cite>) criers with bucinæ and Shofar.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 29:4">Lev. R. s. 29</cite>; Pesik. Baḥod. p. 152ᵃ; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 645:2">Yalk. Lev. 645</cite>; Num. 782; Ps. 840 (corr. acc.). [<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 81:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXXI, 4</cite> <he>ספק ידים</he>, read <he>קרנות ב׳ וסלפינגין</he>.]
